headline: Polymer simulations link chromatin folding to H3K9me3 memory and Xist regulation
label: Chromatin Polymer Physics Modeling
summary: Mechanistic polymer models now simulate epigenetic memory restoration and Xist/Tsix reorganization during X inactivation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is mechanistic polymer modeling of chromatin that links three-dimensional genome organization to epigenetic states. Both preprints apply simulation to specific regulatory outcomes. The first combines polymer biophysics, phase condensates, and enzymatic activity to simulate restoration of H3K9me3 in an epigenetic memory model. The second uses multiscale polymer and nucleosome-resolution modeling of the Xic locus to describe loop-extrusion and methylation-driven reorganization of Xist and Tsix during X inactivation. The published Bayesian comparison of 17 kinetochore dynamics models on RPE1 metaphase tracking data addresses mitotic chromosome movement, a different system, and shares only a model-based inference strategy. What is new is explicit coupling of mechanistic simulation to regulatory outcomes such as memory maintenance and X inactivation.
